content: Cefixime is a semisynthetic cephalosporin antibiotic designed for oral use. Its chemical name is (6R,7R)-7-[2-(2-amino-4-thiazolyl)glyoxylamido]-8-oxo-3-vinyl-5-thia-1-azabicyclo[4.2.0]oct-2-ene-2-carboxylic acid, 7^2-(Z)-trihydrate. The molecular weight of cefixime in its trihydrate form is 507.50, and its chemical formula is C16H15N5O7S2·3H2O. The structural formula of cefixime is as follows: The inactive ingredients in Suprax® (cefixime) 400 mg tablets include dibasic calcium phosphate, hypromellose, lactose monohydrate, magnesium stearate, microcrystalline cellulose, polyethylene glycol, pregelatinized starch, titanium dioxide, and triacetin. The inactive ingredients in Suprax® (cefixime) 400 mg capsules include colloidal silicon dioxide, crospovidone, low-substituted hydroxypropyl cellulose, magnesium stearate, and mannitol. The capsule shell contains ferric oxide black, ferric oxide red, gelatin, potassium hydroxide, propylene glycol, shellac, sodium lauryl sulfate, and titanium dioxide. The inactive ingredients in Suprax® (cefixime) chewable tablets (available in 100 mg, 150 mg, or 200 mg strengths) include aspartame, colloidal silicon dioxide, crospovidone, FD&C Red 40 Aluminum Lake, low-substituted hydroxypropyl cellulose, magnesium stearate, mannitol, fantasy flavor permaseal, and tutti frutti flavor. The inactive ingredients in Suprax® (cefixime) powder for oral suspension include colloidal silicon dioxide, sodium benzoate, strawberry flavor, sucralose (only in the 500 mg/5 mL strength), sucrose, and xanthan gum.
